name: STM32WB55REV6
title: Multiprotocol wireless MCU: Cortex-M4 with FPU, Bluetooth 5 and 802.15.4 radio
summary: The STM32WB55xx and STM32WB35xx pair a 64 MHz Cortex-M4 application core with a Cortex-M0+ that runs a 2.4 GHz radio for Bluetooth 5 (1 and 2 Mbps) and IEEE 802.15.4 (Thread, Zigbee 3.0). They carry up to 1 Mbyte of flash and 256 Kbytes of SRAM (STM32WB35xx: 512 Kbytes and 96 Kbytes), an on-chip step-down converter, a 12-bit 4.26 Msps ADC, comparators, an LCD driver and touch sensing on the WB55, USB full speed and hardware cryptography. They run from 1.71 V to 3.6 V, with -96 dBm BLE sensitivity, up to +6 dBm output and 13 nA in Shutdown. STM32WB55REV6 is the VFQFPN68 version with 512 Kbytes of flash for -40 to 85 °C.

operation.text: An application Cortex-M4 (CPU1) hosts the user program while a separate Cortex-M0+ (CPU2) inside the RF subsystem runs the low layers of the BLE and 802.15.4 stacks, so CPU1 only exchanges high-level messages. Flash, SRAM1, SRAM2a/2b, RNG, AES1, PKA, the clock controller and power control are shared; the two cores talk through the IPCC (six bidirectional channels) and coordinate shared blocks with the hardware semaphores (HSEM). The device always boots on CPU1.

CPU1 is a Cortex-M4 with single-precision FPU, DSP instructions and an MPU of up to eight regions of eight subregions each (32 bytes to 4 Gbytes), at up to 64 MHz. The ART accelerator, a prefetch queue and branch cache in front of the 64-bit flash, gives the equivalent of zero-wait-state execution up to 64 MHz: about 80 DMIPS, 1.25 DMIPS/MHz (Dhrystone 2.1) and 219.48 CoreMark (3.43 CoreMark/MHz).

Up to 1 Mbyte (STM32WB55xx) or 512 Kbytes (STM32WB35xx), with ECC that corrects single and detects double errors and records the failing address. Option bytes set readout protection: Level 0 none; Level 1 blocks flash access whenever debug, SRAM boot or the bootloader is in use; Level 2 permanently disables debug for both cores, SRAM boot and bootloader selection. Two write-protected areas can be set with 4-Kbyte granularity, and two PCROP execute-only areas with 2-Kbyte granularity, optionally erased when RDP drops from Level 1 to 0. Part of the flash is reserved for CPU2 and hidden from CPU1; both cores can program and erase it on a time-shared basis. A 1-Kbyte (128 double words) OTP area is provided.

STM32WB55xx: up to 192 Kbytes of SRAM1 at 0x2000 0000, then SRAM2a (32 Kbytes at 0x2003 0000, mirrored at 0x1000 0000) and SRAM2b (32 Kbytes at 0x2003 8000, mirrored at 0x1000 8000), both with parity. STM32WB35xx has 32 Kbytes of SRAM1 plus the same SRAM2a and SRAM2b, 96 Kbytes in all. SRAM2a can stay powered in Standby. SRAM2 can be write-protected in 1-Kbyte steps and part of it is reserved for the RF subsystem. All SRAM runs at zero wait states at any clock speed of either core.

Customer storage of BLE and 802.15.4 keys, flash and SRAM partitions reachable only by the RF subsystem, a true random number generator, AES-128/256 accelerators (ECB, CBC, CTR, GCM, GMAC, CCM), a public-key accelerator (modular exponentiation up to 3136-bit modulus; elliptic-curve scalar multiplication, ECDSA sign and verify up to 521 bits), a CRC unit, secure firmware install for the radio stacks and a 96-bit unique ID plus an IEEE 64-bit unique ID. A customer key for AES1 can be held by CPU2 and used by CPU1 without being exposed.

The BOOT0 pin (PH3) together with the BOOT1 option bit chooses user flash, system memory or embedded SRAM at start-up. The system-memory bootloader can load code over USB, UART, I2C or SPI; secure firmware update of the radio stacks is possible from the bootloader and over the air.

The transmitter modulates the carrier directly; the receiver is low-IF. An internal transformer at the RF pin gives a single-ended port close to 50 Ω and a natural band-pass that eases harmonic filtering. Output power is set by the LDO voltage of the power amplifier, programmable up to +6 dBm in 1 dB steps, with a smooth ramp. The receiver offers a high-performance or a reduced-current mode, with AGC acting at RF and IF. The synthesiser runs from a 32 MHz crystal whose load is trimmed by two on-chip capacitor banks, so no external trimming capacitors are needed. An external PA can be driven (RF_TX_MOD_EXT_PA / EXT_PA_TX on PB0); an IPD companion (MLPF-WB55-01E3 or MLPF-WB55-02E3) is available for the matching.

Bluetooth 5.0 (1 and 2 Mbps), master and slave, several roles at once, with GAP central, peripheral, observer and broadcaster roles, ATT/GATT client and server, security manager, L2CAP and link-layer AES-128. Data length extension (about 800 kbps at application level), LE privacy 1.2 and LE secure connections are supported. With the SMPS, the RF front end draws 8.1 mA at +6 dBm, and CPU1 reaches 53 µA/MHz while the radio runs. The application talks to the stack on CPU2 through a standard API over the IPCC.

A hardware MAC for IEEE 802.15.4-2011, supporting Thread and Zigbee 3.0: address, version, security and frame-type filtering, a 256-byte receive FIFO (up to eight frames with timing, RSSI and LQI), a 128-byte transmit FIFO that keeps its contents for retries, automatic acknowledgement with programmable delay, full CSMA-CA, a superframe timer, beaconing (needs the LSE), registers retained down to Standby, and an autonomous sniffer woken by timer or CPU2.

An on-chip SMPS step-down converter supplies the core regulators when VDD is high enough. It comes out of reset in bypass; software can switch it on or back to bypass at any time (for example for precise ADC readings), and in its intelligent mode it bypasses itself when VDD falls below a chosen BOR level (BOR1 to BOR4, 2.0 V by default). Without the SMPS, VDDSMPS, VLXSMPS and VFBSMPS are simply wired to VDD. The SMPS needs L1 (2.2 µH at 8 MHz or 10 µH at 4 MHz) and 4.7 µF on VFBSMPS; below 1.95 V VDD it must be forced to bypass (BORH) or left off.

VDD 1.71 V to 3.6 V feeds the I/Os, regulators, radio, SMPS, reset and clocks; VDDRF and VDDSMPS are always tied to VDD. VDDA 1.62 V to 3.6 V (ADC and comparators; 2.4 V minimum for VREFBUF) can differ from VDD and is tied to VDD when unused. VDDUSB 3.0 V to 3.6 V powers the USB transceiver and, when USB is selected, PA11 and PA12; tie it to VDD when unused. VLCD 2.5 V to 3.6 V comes from the pin or from the internal step-up converter, which can reach 3.6 V when VDD exceeds 2.0 V (STM32WB55xx only). VBAT 1.55 V to 3.6 V keeps the LSE, RTC and backup registers alive.

While VDD is below 1 V, VDDA, VDDUSB and VLCD must stay below VDD + 300 mV; above 1 V the supplies are independent. During power-down VDD may briefly drop below the others only if the energy delivered to the chip stays under 1 mJ, which lets decoupling capacitors discharge at different rates.

Three linear regulators feed the logic and radio: the main regulator (Run, Sleep, Stop 0), the low-power regulator (Low-power run, Low-power sleep, Stop 1, Stop 2 and SRAM2a retention in Standby) and the RF regulator, which the RF subsystem manages itself. All three are off in Standby and Shutdown. Range 1 allows CPU clocks up to 64 MHz; Range 2 limits the CPU and all peripheral clocks to 16 MHz (HSE may still run). In Low-power run the CPU is limited to 2 MHz and the radio is unavailable. Flash programming needs Range 1.

A brown-out reset is active in every mode except Shutdown and holds the device in reset below its threshold, so no external reset circuit is needed. BOR0 (about 1.66 V rising) is the power-on level; four higher BOR levels are selectable by option byte. A programmable voltage detector compares VDD with seven thresholds (2.0 V to 2.9 V) and interrupts on either crossing; PVM1 watches VDDUSB and PVM3 watches VDDA. The chosen BOR level can also switch the SMPS to bypass automatically.

After reset the device runs in Run, Range 1. Sleep stops only CPU1; peripherals and the radio keep running. Low-power run runs CPU1 at up to 2 MHz from the low-power regulator, from flash or SRAM, with the radio off; Low-power sleep stops CPU1 from there. Stop 0, 1 and 2 keep all SRAM and registers with the LSE or LSI running and the RTC optionally on; Stop 2 puts most of the core domain into low leakage, Stop 1 keeps more peripherals and wakes faster than Stop 2, and Stop 0 keeps the main regulator on for the fastest wake-up. The radio can wait for events in any Stop mode. Wake-up from Stop uses MSI (up to 48 MHz) or HSI16, and must use HSI16 when the radio or SMPS is in use; the SMPS restarts by itself. The RF subsystem changes its own power state as it needs, and the device settles at the higher of the two cores' demands.

Standby turns the core domain off with the BOR still active; SRAM1, SRAM2b and registers are lost except the backup domain and Standby logic, SRAM2a can be kept (32 Kbytes) and each I/O can be pulled up, pulled down or left floating. It exits on NRST, IWDG, a WKUP pin edge, an RTC event, an LSE failure or the radio, and restarts from HSI16 at 16 MHz; the radio can be used. Shutdown also drops the BOR, so there is no supply monitoring and no switch to the backup domain; all SRAM is lost, it exits on NRST, a WKUP pin edge or an RTC event, restarts from MSI at 4 MHz, and the radio does not operate. Five pins can wake the device from Standby or Shutdown: PA0, PC13, PC12, PA2 and PC5 (two on STM32WB35xx).

During and after reset the I/Os sit in analog state with their Schmitt triggers off to save current, and the NRST pull-up is disconnected when the reset comes from inside. NRST has a 25 kΩ to 55 kΩ pull-up and filters pulses below 70 ns; pulses longer than 350 ns are always taken.

VBAT powers the RTC, LSE and backup registers from a battery, a supercapacitor or VDD, and takes over automatically when VDD is absent; three tamper pins remain active. An internal charger (5 kΩ or 1.5 kΩ) can charge the VBAT source while VDD is present. On VBAT alone, external interrupts and RTC events do not end VBAT operation. VBAT can be measured by the ADC through an internal divide-by-3 bridge.

Sources: LSE 32.768 kHz crystal (four drive levels, or bypass with an external clock); LSI1 32 kHz low-power RC (±5 %); LSI2 high-stability RC near 32 kHz used by the radio; HSE 32 MHz crystal with trimming, required by the radio; HSI16 16 MHz factory-trimmed RC (±1 %); MSI 100 kHz to 48 MHz in twelve steps, auto-trimmed by the LSE to better than ±0.25 %; HSI48 for crystal-less USB, trimmed by the CRS from USB SOF, the LSE or CRS_SYNC. SYSCLK comes from HSI16, MSI, HSE or the PLL (64 MHz maximum); two PLLs with three outputs each also clock the ADC, RNG, SAI and USB. AHB and both APBs run at up to 64 MHz. The device restarts on MSI at 4 MHz. The clock security system switches to HSI16 if HSE fails and can also flag an LSE failure. MCO outputs an internal clock (LSI and LSE down to Stop 1) and LSCO outputs LSI or LSE in all modes down to Standby.

The 32 MHz crystal is specified for NX2016SA and NX1612SA references: 6 pF to 8 pF load, 100 Ω maximum ESR, total tolerance within 50 ppm for BLE or 40 ppm for 802.15.4 (or both). The internal capacitor banks (XOTUNE) pull the frequency by ±20 ppm to ±40 ppm in steps of about 1 ppm to compensate the board; see AN5165 for trimming. Instead of a crystal, a 32 MHz sine of 0.4 V to 1.6 V peak-to-peak can be fed AC-coupled through 470 pF to 100 nF.

The crystal and its load capacitors go as close to the oscillator pins as possible; no resistor may be placed between OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT. The driver strength (LSEDRV) sets the maximum crystal gm the oscillator can start (0.5 µA/V to 2.7 µA/V) and its current (250 nA to 630 nA). Start-up takes about 2 s and depends strongly on the crystal. In bypass the oscillator is off and OSC32_IN takes a 21.2 kHz to 44.4 kHz external clock at I/O levels.

Each GPIO is set by software as a push-pull or open-drain output, a plain or pulled input, or an alternate function, and most carry digital or analog functions. GPIO toggling is fast because the ports sit on AHB2. The alternate-function setting can be locked. Up to 72 I/Os, 70 of them 5 V tolerant. Outputs sink or source ±8 mA, or ±20 mA with relaxed VOL/VOH, within the package totals. I/O structure codes: FT 5 V tolerant, TT 3.6 V tolerant, RF radio, RST reset; suffix _f Fm+ capable, _l LCD function powered from VLCD, _u USB function powered from VDDUSB, _a analog switch powered from VDDA (the TSC switch is powered from VDD). Unless noted, I/Os come out of reset as analog inputs.

An input held at an intermediate voltage draws current through its Schmitt trigger, and a floating input can drift there or toggle with noise. Unused pins and ADC inputs are therefore set to analog mode, or given a defined level by a pull resistor or by making them outputs. Inputs with a pull-up held low draw current through the 40 kΩ typical pull-up.

operation.topic: PC13 to PC15 and PB0, PB1
operation.text: PC13, PC14 and PC15 are fed through the backup power switch, which can sink only 3 mA, so as outputs they are limited to 2 MHz into 30 pF and cannot source current. After a backup-domain power-up their function follows RTC registers that a system reset leaves alone. PB0 and PB1 sit next to the radio: switching above 32 kHz can degrade RF, so their output speed is kept at 00 during RF operation; they are TT pins and accept no positive injection.

SWJ-DP combines JTAG and serial-wire debug; SWD needs only SWDIO (PA13) and SWCLK (PA14), freeing the other JTAG pins for GPIO, and a sequence on TMS switches between the two ports. After reset PA13, PA14, PA15, PB3 and PB4 are in their debug roles, with pull-ups on PA13, PA15 and PB4 and a pull-down on PA14. The Embedded Trace Macrocell streams compressed instruction and data trace over the TRACE pins to an external trace port analyser.

Two DMA controllers with seven channels each; the DMAMUX can route any peripheral request to any channel and add hardware triggers. Channels have four software priority levels, independent source and destination widths, circular buffers, half/complete/error flags, and move up to 65536 items between memory and peripherals in any direction.

The NVIC handles up to 63 maskable interrupt channels plus the 16 core interrupt lines with 16 priority levels. The EXTI turns configurable or direct events into wake-up requests, interrupts and events for either core.

One 12-bit successive-approximation ADC with built-in calibration (recommended after each power-up): 4.26 Msps at 12 bits, up to 7.11 Msps at 6 bits, sampling times down to 39 ns, up to 16 bits through 256x hardware oversampling. Up to 16 external channels, single-ended or differential, plus internal channels for VREFINT (ADC1_IN0), the temperature sensor (ADC1_IN17) and VBAT/3. Consumption scales with conversion rate (about 200 µA/Msps); the ADC clock is independent of the CPU clock. Two conversion groups (regular and injected), multiple timer and external triggers, three analog watchdogs, DMA and offset compensation are provided. Below VDDA = 2.4 V the I/O analog switch booster must be enabled. On UFQFPN48 VREF+ is VDDA.

The source impedance RAIN (50 kΩ maximum) and the pad plus board capacitance must charge the 5 pF sample capacitor within the sampling time; the sampling-time table gives the minimum for each RAIN. A large parasitic capacitance degrades accuracy, which a lower ADC clock recovers. VDDA decoupling follows the supply scheme, with the 10 nF ceramic capacitor right at the chip. Negative current injected on any analog pin disturbs conversions on other channels.

The temperature sensor gives a voltage rising about 2.5 mV/°C (0.76 V at 30 °C), read through ADC1_IN17 with at least 5 µs sampling. Each part is calibrated in production: TS_CAL1 (30 °C) at 0x1FFF 75A8 and TS_CAL2 (130 °C) at 0x1FFF 75CA, both taken at VDDA = VREF+ = 3.0 V. The internal reference VREFINT (1.212 V typ) feeds the ADC and comparators; its value measured at 30 °C and VDDA = VREF+ = 3.6 V is stored at 0x1FFF 75AA.

On STM32WB55xx the voltage reference buffer outputs 2.048 V or 2.5 V on VREF+ for the ADC and outside parts, with 0.5 µF to 1.5 µF load (including 100 nF) and up to 4 mA. When it is off, an external reference can drive VREF+. On UFQFPN48 VREF+ is bonded to VDDA, so the buffer has no pin there.

Two rail-to-rail comparators with selectable speed and power, hysteresis and output polarity. The inverting input can be an I/O or VREFINT or one of its fractions (1/4, 1/2, 3/4). They can wake the device from Stop, interrupt, trigger timer breaks and pair up as a window comparator.

Up to 18 capacitive channels on STM32WB55xx (6 on VFQFPN68, none on UFQFPN48 and on STM32WB35xx) using surface charge transfer, with up to six channels acquired in parallel, spread spectrum, programmable charge frequency and max-count error detection. One sampling capacitor serves up to three channels of a group; the STMTouch library supports it.

STM32WB55xx drives up to 8x40 or 4x44 segments (4x28 on VFQFPN68, 4x13 on UFQFPN48) with static, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 and 1/8 duty and static, 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4 bias, double-buffered display RAM, blinking and contrast control. An internal step-up converter can make VLCD above VDD (up to 3.6 V when VDD > 2.0 V); it then needs a capacitor of about 1 µF from VLCD to ground. Unused segment and common pins remain GPIOs. The display stays on through Sleep, the two low-power run/sleep modes and Stop.

TIM1 is a 16-bit advanced timer with four channels, three complementary outputs, dead time and break inputs; TIM2 is a 32-bit timer with four channels and quadrature encoder support; TIM16 and TIM17 are 16-bit with one channel and one complementary output each. LPTIM1 and LPTIM2 are 16-bit low-power timers clocked from LSE, LSI, HSI16, APB or an external input, able to count and wake the device in Stop (LPTIM1 down to Stop 2, LPTIM2 down to Stop 1; encoder mode on LPTIM1). The independent watchdog (12-bit, LSI clocked) runs in Stop and Standby; the window watchdog (7-bit) runs from the main clock with an early-warning interrupt; SysTick is a 24-bit down-counter.

A BCD calendar RTC with sub-seconds, two alarms, a 17-bit periodic wake-up timer, timestamp, three tamper inputs, 0.95 ppm digital calibration, shift correction and a 50/60 Hz reference input. It is clocked from the LSE, LSI1/LSI2 or HSE/32. Twenty 32-bit backup registers (80 bytes) survive system reset and wake-up from Standby or Shutdown and are powered from VDD or VBAT. Clocked by the LSE the RTC works in all modes including VBAT; clocked by an LSI it works in every mode except Shutdown and VBAT.

Two I2C (I2C1, I2C3) with Standard, Fast and Fast-mode Plus (1 Mbit/s, 20 mA drive), SMBus/PMBus, an independent clock and wake from Stop on address match (I2C3 also from Stop 2). One USART up to 4 Mbit/s with IrDA, LIN, smartcard, Modbus, RS485 driver enable and SPI master mode, waking from Stop at up to 200 kbaud. One LPUART that wakes from Stop at up to 220 kbaud and runs up to 9600 baud from the LSE alone. Two SPI (one on STM32WB35xx) up to 32 Mbit/s master and 24 Mbit/s slave, 4- to 16-bit frames, TI mode and CRC. One SAI with two sub-blocks for I2S, PCM, TDM, AC'97 and SPDIF, and a PDM interface for up to three digital microphone pairs. A Quad-SPI interface (SDR and DDR) maps external flash into memory for execute-in-place. One USB 2.0 full-speed device with crystal-less operation (HSI48 + CRS, -15 °C to 85 °C), BCD and LPM, internal DP pull-up and no external series resistors.

One address space is shared by both cores. Parts of the flash and of SRAM2a/2b are secure and reachable only by CPU2. Shared blocks such as RCC, PWR, EXTI and the flash interface need software arbitration, which the HSEM can provide. The full map is in reference manual RM0434.

Unless stated, voltages are referred to VSS. Min and max values are guaranteed at worst-case temperature, supply and frequency by production tests at 25 °C and TAmax; values from characterization are mean ±3σ. Typical values are at 25 °C and VDD = VDDA = 3 V. Typical ADC accuracy covers 95 % of parts (mean ±2σ). Pin parameters are measured with 50 pF load. RF figures are given up to 85 °C.

Every supply pair (VDD/VSS, VDDA/VSSA and so on) is decoupled with ceramic capacitors as in the supply scheme, placed at the pins or directly underneath on the far side of the board. On UFBGA129 the DCAP ball pairs carry the 100 nF capacitors and are tied inside to VDD and VSS, so the supply can enter at the centre of the array on the bottom layer of a two-layer board without breaking the ground plane. The exposed pad of the QFN packages must go to the ground plane for the radio to work.

Supply current figures are taken with all I/Os in analog mode, peripherals off unless listed, the minimum flash wait states for the clock, and fPCLK = fHCLK. Typical current is about 107 µA/MHz in Run (Range 1), 53 µA/MHz with the SMPS and radio, 13 nA in Shutdown, 600 nA in Standby with RTC and 32 KB SRAM, and 2.1 µA in Stop 2 with RTC and all SRAM; radio Rx 4.5 mA and Tx 5.2 mA at 0 dBm with the SMPS.

Tested with IEC 61000-4-2 ESD on the I/Os (class 2B) and IEC 61000-4-4 fast bursts through 100 pF on VDD and VSS (class 5A); emission (IEC 61967-2, WLCSP100) is EMI level 1.5. HBM ESD is 2000 V; CDM 500 V (250 V on UFBGA129); latch-up class II at 105 °C.

TJ must stay within the general operating conditions. Suffix 6 parts are rated for TA up to 85 °C at full dissipation (TJ 105 °C) and suffix 7 for 105 °C (TJ 125 °C); at low dissipation the ambient may extend by 20 °C while TJ stays in range. ΘJA is 24.9 °C/W for UFQFPN48, 47.0 °C/W for VFQFPN68, 35.8 °C/W for WLCSP100 and 41.5 °C/W for UFBGA129 (JESD51-2, still air).

UFBGA129: 7 x 7 mm, 0.5 mm pitch, 129 balls. WLCSP100: 4.40 x 4.38 mm, 0.4 mm pitch, 100 balls. VFQFPN68: 8 x 8 mm, 0.4 mm pitch, exposed pad 6.4 mm. UFQFPN48: 7 x 7 mm, 0.5 mm pitch, exposed pad 5.6 mm, which must be soldered to ground; all its leads should also be soldered for joint life. All packages are ECOPACK2. Recommended pads: UFBGA129 0.36 mm pad, 0.46 mm solder mask opening, 0.36 mm stencil 0.1 mm thick; WLCSP100 0.225 mm pad, 0.29 mm mask, 0.25 mm stencil 0.1 mm thick.
